business_problem: Pennsylvania wanted to reduce time spent on drafting, research, summarization, IT support, procurement, contract analysis, and other administrative work across state agencies while keeping human oversight, transparency, and labor protections in place for government use of generative AI.
solution_summary: The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, through the Office of Administration, ran a year-long generative AI pilot that gave 175 employees in 14 agencies access to ChatGPT Enterprise for real government workflows. Staff used the service for writing, research, document summarization, IT support, contract analysis, policy research, stakeholder communications, software-upgrade work, and training-content development. The implementation was governed by Executive Order 2023-19 and oversight bodies created for responsible AI use, while Carnegie Mellon University researchers collaborated on evaluation. Rather than embedding AI into a back-end transaction system, the pilot served as a secure end-user productivity layer: employees brought work materials and prompts into ChatGPT Enterprise, received drafts or summaries back, and then applied human review before use. Adoption was supported with prompt training, biweekly feedback sessions, interviews, and live demonstrations to measure impact and improve rollout.

solution_components.name: ChatGPT Enterprise
solution_components.role: Provided the generative AI workspace state employees used for writing, research, summarization, IT support, and other day-to-day productivity tasks during the pilot.

data_flow: Employees in 14 Pennsylvania agencies entered prompts and work materials such as emails, long documents, contracts, policy questions, and software-support tasks into ChatGPT Enterprise. The system returned drafts, summaries, research assistance, and troubleshooting help to those employees, who reviewed outputs before using them in government workflows. OA then collected biweekly feedback, interviews, and live demonstrations to assess impact and refine adoption.
business_outcome: The pilot showed strong employee acceptance and measurable productivity gains, with faster drafting, summarization, hiring-related work, procurement, contract review, policy research, and software-upgrade support, while reinforcing that AI should augment rather than replace government workers.
metrics: average time savings of 95 minutes per day

architecture_clues: Pilot ran for about one year across 14 state agencies.
Office of Administration collaborated with Carnegie Mellon University Block Center for Technology and Society throughout the pilot.
Results were collected through biweekly feedback sessions, user interviews, and live demonstrations.
Governance was anchored by Executive Order 2023-19 and a Generative AI Governing Board.
The Administration also established a Generative AI Labor and Management Collaboration Group for ongoing oversight.
evidence_quotes: "the pilot program provided state employees with access to ChatGPT Enterprise to enhance efficiency, streamline workflows, and improve the delivery of services for Pennsylvanians."
"employees had a highly positive experience, reporting an average time savings of 95 minutes per day while using ChatGPT for writing, research, summarization, and IT support."
"Over the course of a year, 175 employees from 14 agencies used ChatGPT Enterprise to test AI’s impact."
"Nearly half of the participants, 48 percent, had never used ChatGPT before, yet over 85 percent reported a 'somewhat positive' or 'very positive' experience"
"AI-assisted work helped employees improve hiring timelines, streamline procurement, more quickly analyze contracts, and research new policies faster."
"Employees emphasized that AI augments human expertise rather than replacing it, reinforcing the importance of human review and judgment."
